articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

fullParagraphs: Oil prices fell at Monday’s (November 9, 2026) open after U.S. President ​Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ‌attackswhile talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both ​nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ⁠the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or ‌0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel.

The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s (November 6, 2026) settlement as the market assessed the ‌possibility of further U.S. strikes on Iran, although Brent fell ‌17% ⁠last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start ⁠of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988.
“It depends on whether or not they sign ​a very strong agreement,” Trump ‌told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.”

Mr. Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s U.S. midterm elections , but there has ‌been no sign of a large-scale U.S. military operation. ​Iran has said it would respond by striking U.S. and Israeli targets.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM ⁠Trade, called Mr. Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market is still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s ‌approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.”

Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering West Asian oil flows, rising production from other countries and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday (November 6, 2026), estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels ‌per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), ​Iraq reached an understanding with the U.S. to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via ⁠a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an ⁠interview with Al Jazeera.
He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 ‌billion.
Separately the Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital Riyadh on Sunday that left windows ​blown out but no reported casualties.

articles.title: New Israeli parliament to take aim at Netanyahu as Eisenkot seeks government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israel's new parliament convened on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with plans to take aim immediately at caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to quickly cobble together a new government.

Mr. Eisenkot, leading a broad left-to-right bloc, will control the agenda from the outset in the new parliament with the help of Israeli-Arab parties, although neither he nor the right-wing Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, hold a majority on their own.

"I am committed in this complex situation to form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible," Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief who only recently entered politics, said before his swearing-in.
President Isaac Herzog, ceremonially opening the session, called on all sides to work together and avoid a fresh election in a deeply polarised country weary from three years of war.
"Nearly 80% of the people went to the polls and elected you. You must do everything to avoid a repeat election," Mr. Herzog said.
"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals."

Mr. Eisenkot's allies hope to use their newfound legislative power to move rapidly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israel's history.
ALSO WATCH Israel’s Eisenkot invites Netanyahu to join government under his leadership

Mr. Herzog on Sunday (November 8, 2026) gave Mr. Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to piece together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

Hours before the opening of the Parliament, known as the Knesset, Mr. Eisenkot's party announced agreements on key people to replace allies of Mr. Netanyahu, who has been in and out of office for nearly 20 years.
Mr. Eisenkot's bloc announced it had the votes to install as parliament speaker Matan Kahana, a former senior military figure who clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews during a past stint in government.
Avigdor Liberman, a right-wing member of Eisenkot's bloc who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee.

fullParagraphs: The European Union ’s (EU) top climate official admitted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that expectations were "low" from the COP31 summit in Turkiye, while holding out hope for "meaningful" progress on the topic of clean electricity.

"Expectations are low — that's just a reflection of reality," European Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told a group of reporters including from AFP , arguing that electrification should be the core focus of the United Nations climate talks .
"If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," he said.

The European commissioner will travel to the Turkish resort of Antalya on Monday (November 9, 2026) for the talks which run until November 20. Mr. Hoekstra voiced hope that setting an electrification target would be "at the heart" of the summit conclusions, adding: "Of course, the cleaner that electrification is, the better it is."
ALSO WATCH COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains

Host nation Turkiye is inviting countries to join a voluntary "electrification" pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20% today to 35% by 2035. But the EU's call for "clean" electrification could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.
Observers expect few major breakthroughs from COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the U.S. war with Iran and Russia's conflict in Ukraine.
The talks are also missing a major player since U.S. President Donald Trump who pulled Washington out of the Paris climate agreement has not sent officials to the talks.

"The larger picture is that the geopolitics of the times we live in are extremely complicated," said Mr. Hoekstra, who acknowledged that a string of recent COP meetings had been "underwhelming in terms of their delivery".
"There are substantial questions to be asked on how fit for purpose this design actually still is, with its unanimity" system that does not always deliver "what is actually needed," he said.

The EU has previously warned there would be no political will for extra funding pledges at COP31, a message Mr. Hoekstra repeated. "Europe is at the absolute top of delivering on climate finance, not just for ourselves but also for others," Mr. Hoekstra said, calling for a push for "more burden sharing".

Environmental groups have criticised a series of recent European rollbacks on climate, most lately plans to postpone rules targeting methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas. But Mr. Hoekstra pushed back at the notion the EU was backsliding on its ambitions.

articles.title: Iran rejects France’s ‘baseless accusations’ on cyberattack
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Iran on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were “baseless”.
“Iran’s Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France,” the Ministry said in a statement.
It added that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.
Similar incidents were then reported in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

Along with summoning Iran’s ambassador and seeking European-level sanctions, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Tuesday that Paris would “rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks”.
Tehran meanwhile said it would “not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities”.
It added that France “is merely projecting its own governance failures” with these accusations.
“A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations,” it continued.
Also on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the European Union said it would look to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states after France’s announcement.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. court allows Pannun to serve NSA Doval and former intelligence chief Goyal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A U.S. court on Monday (November 9, 2026) allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to serve his civil plea on National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel through Indian judicial channels, after the State Department submitted that it had served the notice for the two officials at the Indian Embassy in Washington.
The Ministry of External Affairs rejected the move, saying such judicial documents must be sent to the Ministry of Law and Justice in India. It called the lawsuit “frivolous”.

The lawsuit filed by Mr. Pannun, wanted in India on terror charges, is separate but linked to the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) findings of an assassination plot against him in June 2023. An undercover Drug Enforcement Agency informant had pointed to Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, and to conversations with senior Indian intelligence officials, including Vikash Yadav, regarding a conspiracy to hire a hitman to kill Mr. Pannun in New York.

Mr. Gupta pleaded guilty to the charges, and the U.S. courts have scheduled the sentencing for November 20. Mr. Yadav was arrested in Delhi in December 2023 on separate charges by Indian authorities and was given bail in April 2024.

The FBI and Canadian officials, who are investigating a similar case involving the killing of separatist Harjeet Singh Nijjar in Vancouver in June 2023, appear to have dropped earlier claims of the involvement of more senior officials, including Mr. Doval, Mr. Goel and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. However, Mr. Pannun sought to pursue his case further and filed several petitions demanding that the court summon Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel. In February 2025, when Mr. Doval accompanied Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Washington for a bilateral visit and meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump, Mr. Pannun had tried to serve the NSA with a notice and failed.

The Ministry of External Affairs indicated on Tuesday (November 10) that it was unconcerned by the latest development in the case and that the procedure for issuing the notice would require engaging the Law Ministry directly, not via the Embassy or the MEA.

“We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials, as also we reject the frivolous lawsuits. Request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India’s designated central authority, that is the Ministry of Law and Justice,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to questions at a regular briefing.

Granting permission for the summons on Monday (November 9), U.S. District Judge Katherine Polk Failla directed Mr. Pannun to prepare documents on or before November 30, including the summons addressed to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel, details of Indian law and procedure, and the route by which the summons would be issued, as well as records of previous attempts at serving the two officials under the Hague Convention.

The certificate of submission delivered to the Indian Embassy by the State Department was signed by an official and dated October 9, 2026. The State Department said in a footnote that the delivery did not mean it was taking a “position” on the case and it was a “legal obligation.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold first Pentagon briefing since May amid impeachment threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to give his first news conference from the Pentagon in six months on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), just a day after a Republican lawmaker launched an effort to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war against Iran and other actions.

The briefing will be Mr. Hegseth's first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America.

Mr. Hegseth, who has said the news conference would focus on the impeachment threat, is gearing up for a fight, having launched a social media blitz and saying he is ready to defend his and President Donald Trump's actions from “politically motivated people.”

Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican who lost his primary to a Trump-backed opponent, filed the impeachment resolution in the House on Monday (November 9). It sets the stage for a dramatic vote on whether to remove a prominent Trump administration figure following sweeping losses for Republicans in last week's midterm elections that many at least partly blamed on the Iran conflict and its economic impact.

The resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Mr. Hegseth's role in military actions in Yemen against Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela. Massie said Hegseth's actions amount to “high crimes and misdemeanors” and his leadership at the Pentagon “warrants impeachment.”
A vote in the House could come by midweek, putting pressure on Republicans — many of whom blamed their election wipeout on the Iran war — but next steps are highly uncertain.

Mr. Trump has backed Hegseth, pointing to the raid to capture then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January as well as military operations against Iran that he asserts have “obliterated” its navy and air force.

Iran, however, has been able to keep striking U.S. military bases in West Asia and has disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz during the course of the more than 8-month-old conflict, driving up global oil prices. Mr. Trump told reporters on Monday (November 9) that the Iran war “militarily is effectively over" and repeated his often-made claim that Iran “would love to make a deal.”
Mr. Hegseth also has been defending his stewardship of the U.S. military.

“There's a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success,” he told reporters on Monday (November 10) after a speech at the Naval War College in Rhode Island. He added that “if we want to litigate” the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, “I'm happy to do it all day long.”
He also released a video on social media last week that argued impeachment would be “all about the politics of personal destruction” and that “won't work with me. You can rest assured of that.”
Afterward, scores of Pentagon political appointees posted images of Hegseth emblazoned with the words, “Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic.”

articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Forty-eight hours before Deepavali, amidst the rising crescendo of crackers heralding the festivities, a Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the people, and not the judiciary, must strike a blow against air pollution in the national capital.

Instead, the court went beyond Deepavali to highlight a consistent danger that sustains and would worsen the toxic air: vehicular emissions. On November 6, the court detected a sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions.

It told the authorities that the thick smog, which later raised the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) to almost the ‘severe’ category following Deepavali, had nowhere to go in the landlocked capital. The substantial commercial and non-commercial traffic entering Delhi would only compound the problem in the coming days.

“It must be borne in mind that Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), by virtue of their geographical and economic interconnectedness, bear the cumulative burden of vehicular traffic originating not merely within their own boundaries but also from the neighbouring States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan,” the Supreme Court reminded the authorities in its latest order.

The issue warranted urgent and immediate intervention, the court said, directing the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), the Delhi government, the Delhi Police (Traffic department), as well as the neighbouring States of Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh to file their responses on what they have done to regulate in the national capital the entry and plying of commercial and non-commercial vehicles.

The court wanted to know about measures to regulate traffic originating from outside the national capital. These include steps taken to identify, monitor, and regulate vehicles that do not conform to prescribed emission standards, and measures to prevent the entry and operation of overage, end-of-life, or non-compliant vehicles.

The Bench has specifically sought information on the measures undertaken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry, and the coordination mechanisms between the authorities of Delhi and the neighbouring States for regulating inter-State vehicular movement.

The court has asked if the authorities have any “further short-term and long-term measures proposed or contemplated to mitigate vehicular emissions and reduce their contribution to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and the National Capital Region”.

Incidentally, two separate orders of the Supreme Court passed several months ago, on January 21 and February 23 this year, had contained detailed long-term and short-term measures recommended by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to mitigate air pollution, especially caused by vehicular emissions, in Delhi.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, for CAQM, had, at the time, submitted that a meta-analysis of studies from 2015 to 2025 attributed PM2.5 in Delhi to a mix of primary emissions and secondary particulate formation from sources within the national capital region itself. The measures suggested by the CAQM included developing multi-modal transport hubs connecting the metro, Regional Rapid Transit System, and last-mile connectivity with a real-time passenger information system, higher incentives to owners for scrapping old vehicles, expansion in EV charging infrastructure, etc.

“We direct the concerned agencies, particularly, the MCD, to submit their immediate response as to why these measures be not implemented without any delay. Once again, we clarify that no objections will be entertained against the recommendations made by the CAQM,” the court had made its intent clear on January 21.

articles.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday (November 9, 2026) that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
“I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape,” Mr. Trump said at a White House briefing.

The sudden emergence of Mr. Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence.

Mr. Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Mr. Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Mr. Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

Mr. Huang -- a singular figure in the technology landscape and one of the world's wealthiest people -- has acknowledged that he had an affair, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.

“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security,” Mr. Huang said in his letter.
Nvidia announced Sunday (November 8, 2026) it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Mr. Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The episode is also attracting congressional scrutiny, with top Democrats Sen. Mark Warner and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries saying on Monday (November 9, 2026) that they are interested in investigating it further. Jeffries said the Nvidia issue came up during a closed-door session with the CIA director and the Director of National Intelligence that was primarily about Iran.

“We're going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened,” he said, “and what the implications are in terms of America's national security.”

Mr. Trump is slated to meet next week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but he was noncommittal about bringing up the situation with Mr. Xi.
“No, I don't think so,” Mr. Trump said. “I mean, maybe. I'm sure President XI will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he's a very honourable man.”

articles.title: Kadambini Ganguly: breaking barriers in medicine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Have you heard of the names Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi? Considered India’s first female doctors, these names have often been looked past in the pages of history and even medical textbooks. Today, let’s talk about the story of Kadambini Ganguly — India’s first practising lady doctor.

It was in 1861 that Brahmo reformer and headmaster Braja Kishore Basu had a daughter. She was named Kadambini Basu. Young Kadambini, despite hailing from a community that did not necessarily support women’s education like many others at the time did, received an education at the Brahmo Eden Female School and later at the Hindu Mahila Vidyalaya.

As the daughter of someone who organised and fought for women’s emancipation, Kadambini went on to study in college and became the first woman to pass the University of Calcutta entrance examination. In 1882, she passed the examination for the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree along with Chandramukhi Basu from the University of Calcutta, making her and Chandramukhi the first female graduates in the country.

Wanting to study medicine, Kadambini decided to enrol at the Calcutta Medical College after graduation. She was, however, believed to have been unable to receive the BMC certificate due to a shortage of a couple of marks. She did receive the GBMC (Graduate of Bengal Medical College) degree, though, in 1886. Thus, she became the first Indian woman to be allowed to practice Western medicine.

Around 1888, Kadambini started working at the Lady Dufferin Hospital for a monthly salary of 300 rupees. She had even gone to Nepal to treat British royalty. Along with pursuing medicine, she was also politically quite vocal and active. Around 1899, Kadambini was one of the first women delegates elected to the Fifth Session of the Congress in Bombay and the next year, she won to become the first women speaker at the Congress.

She also served as the president of the Transvaal Indian Association, founded by Gandhiji’s colleague Henry Pollock. She was a member of the Women’s Conference held in Calcutta and even presided over the General Brahmo Samaj session in Calcutta.

Around 1883, Kadambini married Dwarakanath Ganguly (thus the change in name from Kadambini Bose to Kadambini Ganguly in many documents). Dwarakanath Ganguly was a Bengali Brahmo reformer, educator, journalist, and pioneer of women’s rights in British India.

She was a mother to eight children and is often said to have been deft in needlework. She became a practising doctor while equally devoting herself to family and household affairs, an action which was deemed impossible by many in the era.

Despite having being burdened with domestic chores, like most women of that time, Kadambini still managed to smash the glass ceilings and societal stereotypes in both her professional and personal life.
A name which should not be forgotten in the course of time, Dr Kadambini is a reason many of us are able to pursue our passion — in medicine and in life.

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with experts warning that the gaps have led to understated pollution levels and resulted in a lower official air quality index (AQI).

According to Dr. D. Saha, former head of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)’s air quality laboratory, AQI values are calculated using a moving or running average of hourly concentrations of eight parameters, including PM2.5 and PM10, over the previous 24 hours.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), PM2.5 data were missing for several hours at many stations in the city, including Anand Vihar, Patparganj and Bawana, on the CPCB website. PM2.5 (particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter) consists of fine inhalable particles that can penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream, causing respiratory and other diseases. Similar data gaps were reported at several monitoring stations during Deepavali last year as well.

Manoj Kumar, an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finland-based non-profit research organisation, said the missing hourly PM2.5 data “raised concerns about the assessment of Delhi’s air quality”.

“From midnight on November 8 until 5 a.m. on November 9, 227 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation,” Mr. Kumar said, adding, “When the hourly PM2.5 data is missing, it will artificially lower the AQI, showing better air quality when the actual air quality is worse.”

When asked about the missing air quality data at several monitoring stations, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra told the media that the government would look into the issue. The Member Secretary of the CPCB, which releases AQI data, did not respond to calls and messages seeking comment.
Dr. Saha told The Hindu that there should not be gaps in the data, especially during crucial periods.

“If hourly PM2.5 or PM10 value is blank or missing, it will affect the AQI calculated and the final value of the AQI calculated will be less than the actual value of AQI and scientifically incorrect,” Mr. Saha said.

He also said the CPCB had set the measurement range of PM2.5 analysers at 0–1,000 micrograms per cubic metre, which meant they could not measure concentrations above that level. “So, if the value of PM2.5 is beyond 1,000, it should at least be shown as 1,000 instead of showing blank,” he said.

A former DPCC scientist, who did not wish to be identified, said the CPCB recorded PM2.5 values only up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre because there was a minor drop in accuracy at higher levels. “But at very high values, a small drop in accuracy will not matter a lot. Ideally, the CPCB should be measuring the higher values so that we are not missing the peak values,” the official said, adding that not measuring higher concentrations would artificially make air quality appear better.
Bhavreen Kandhari, an environmental activist, alleged that the government was clearly fudging the data to conceal the actual air pollution situation rather than solving the problem.
On the CPCB website, PM2.5 readings appeared to be capped at 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre across all stations, with data missing for several hours at multiple locations.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.
